Remove the orphan spots of one cluster

Source: R/R-clean.R
clean_orphans.Rd

Removes the spots of the cluster that belong to a contiguous piece of fewer than `min_size` spots. Spots of other clusters are always kept.

Usage

clean_orphans(
  df,
  clusters,
  min_size = 20,
  max_dist = NULL,
  coord_cols = c("x", "y"),
  cluster_col = "cluster"
)

Arguments

df

A data.frame with coordinates and a cluster column.

clusters

The cluster to split (a single label).

min_size

Pieces with fewer spots are removed.

max_dist

Maximal distance between touching spots. `NULL` uses 1.5 times the spot spacing (direct grid neighbors).

coord_cols, cluster_col

Names of the coordinate and cluster columns.

Value

`df` without the orphan spots. If every piece is smaller than `min_size`, `df` is returned unchanged with a warning.

Details

To clean border spots, use it on the output of [create_cluster_layers()]: layers are then computed with all spots, and labels are not changed.

See also

[split_clusters()]

Examples

df <- expand.grid(x = 1:20, y = 1:10)
df$spot_id <- paste0("s", seq_len(nrow(df)))
df$cluster <- "B"
df$cluster[df$x <= 4 | df$x >= 18] <- "A"   # two pieces
df$cluster[df$x == 10 & df$y == 5] <- "A"   # one orphan spot
cleaned <- clean_orphans(df, "A", min_size = 5)
nrow(df) - nrow(cleaned)
#> [1] 1

# Clean layers: computed with all spots, then orphans are removed
layers <- create_cluster_layers(df, "A", k = 4)
layers <- clean_orphans(layers, "A", min_size = 5)
table(layers$layer)
#> 
#>       border         core intermediate 
#>           20           10           40
